html:
The Registan is the old central square of Samarkand, framed on three sides by tiled madrasas, or Islamic colleges. Its name means "sandy place".

  • Ulugh Beg Madrasa, built from 1417 by the astronomer prince Ulugh Beg, grandson of Timur, when Samarkand was a capital of the Timurid Empire.
  • Sher-Dor Madrasa, built in the 1620s and 1630s, with tiger-like beasts chasing deer on its gate, an unusual image for Islamic buildings.
  • Tilya-Kori Madrasa, finished around 1660, whose mosque is covered inside in gold.

The two later buildings were raised under the Uzbek khans, who ruled the city after the Timurids. With their huge gateways, domes and blue tilework, the three façades became the classic picture of Central Asian architecture. The square was a market, a place for public announcements and for executions.
